task.title: Relics: measure the history walk when a long relic changes
task.description:
A relic is a record in Workbook beside tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions and similar material as named parts, with the same history and sharing that tasks have.

This is a follow-up from the review of the first six relics stories (finding M66). It was left out of that work on purpose.

## Problem

When a relic's ref moves, the index reads the changes it has not seen. To find them it asks Git for the parent of every commit in that relic's history (`git rev-list --parents`, in `relicParentGraph`), and then reads only the commits after the last one it indexed. So the listing grows with the relic's whole history, while the reading does not. Tasks do the same in `parentGraphFor`.

## Wanted

Measure the cost for a relic with a long history. If it matters, end the listing at the last indexed commit, for relics and for tasks.

## Done when

- The relic benchmark has a scenario that changes a relic with at least 1,000 commits.
- The result says whether the listing needs a stop point, and the change is made if it does.
